question: Can tiny real-observation learned controllers acquire reliable, verifiable CartPole skill under factual expert-demonstration supervision before interpreting P18 reward-only policy collapse as substrate limitation?
null: None of three original learned architectures reaches >=175 real factual CartPole reward/action steps per episode over four new public DEV reset seeds for all 3 model initializations; or genuine-label learned conventional controller not >=50 above same-budget wrongly assigned label negative.

design.environment: real source-verified MIT Farama Gymnasium v1.1.1 CartPole-v1 via original S29 owner admission
design.expert: p18.handcoded_action(obs) sign(theta + 0.5*observed_theta_dot) using only currently public 4D observation and BEFORE true env.step; actual chosen actions and subsequent reward are source recorded. No latent engine physics, hidden state, wind or counterfactual.
design.history: 8 complete factual (4 public sensor, prior action, prior observed reward) rows; only current real sensor plus past factual rows; pads cold first obs
design.optimizer: AdamW supervised cross-entropy 0.008; original executed teacher decision is the factual class label, no reward-only RL objective
design.conventional_linear_model: 4 observed continuous dims to one logit; teacher can be representable with no tokens
design.history_mlp: original P18 471 trainable parameter history MLP and value head, supervised action logits only
design.history_gru: original P18 489 trainable parameter history GRU and value head, supervised action logits only
design.wrong_attribution_negative: same 4D linear model/same 700 update budget with teacher action targets randomly permuted among recorded factual observations, preserve histogram but destroy causal sensor-action association
